items.title: Durable interview-continuation carrier: Name one durable interview-continuation record owned under ./xbrief/plan.xbrief.json (closed field or adjacent plan-owned artifact). Required fields: target deliverable, current phase (closed enum), reopenable decision set, accepted deferrals, confirmation records with scope tags (answer|artifact|phase), limited delta under review, approval target + revision identity. Exclude ephemeral continue-here / continue.xbrief.json as this carrier. Resume MUST load this durable record; incomplete orientation is fail-closed refuse.

Closed phase vocabulary: Closed enum covering at least planning-draft-approved, correction-or-gap-review, artifact-approved, deferred-resume. Free-text phase labels refused. Map onto setup Phase 1/2/3 vocabulary without colliding names.

Approval taxonomy + gate bind-map: Approval scope comes from the explicitly presented gate and its target, never from numeric syntax alone. Map onto existing Rule 6 / Post-Interview / Full Path human approval surfaces.

Operator-enumerated delta reopen: Changing a decision reopens only operator-enumerated keys (Rule 6 L160 shape). Default refuse-to-widen. Additions require explicit operator widen plus recorded dependency reason. Agent-inferred demonstrable dependents are not a widening path. Stop when bounded delta satisfied. Adversarial fixture: refuse unrelated backend improvement as addition.

Handoff authority split with read-side refuse: Mid-review / cross-session handoffs MUST use durable carrier (or structured export), not unlabeled chat prose. Human-authorized constraints require reference/excerpt of operator grant. Agent conventions non-binding unless operator adopts via explicit marker. Incomplete-handoff remediation recovers orientation only.

Authorized incremental recordkeeping: Confirmed state may be recorded under an existing grant without another permission prompt. That grant does not authorize synchronizing unrelated scopes or generating an artifact alongside the next interview question. Keep anti-pattern forbidding combining interview questions with artifact generation.

Evidence / fixtures: Content-contract pins on both pack SoT and rendered skill surfaces. Prefer verify-style assertion against durable carrier after resume. Include: same-session correction; resume after continue-checkpoint consumption with carrier intact; artifact edit after approval (affected invalid; unchanged remains); incomplete handoff refuse; unsupported authorization label refuse; adversarial unrelated-proposal refuse; positive incremental recordkeeping under existing grant.

Landing surfaces: Primary: interview skill (pack + rendered), setup Full output/review / Post-Interview gate pointers, strategies/interview brownfield Update / delta continuation, continue-here.md explicit exclusion + pointer to durable carrier, plan.xbrief.json schema/field docs. Dual-surface pins where pack-render applies. CHANGELOG Unreleased.

design-critique: warranted, because post-draft design-interview corrections and cross-session handoffs do not preserve a bounded phase and approval scope: Rule-8 numeric confirm can become the practical workflow unit while answer approval, artifact approval, and phase completion blur, and agent-authored handoff conventions can expand an indefinite proposal loop.

Dual-stop cap: 6 posts

pain: P1, P2, P3

- P1. Missing phase/continuation state: after an approved planning draft, a correction or gap review and a fresh-session resume lack durable fields for deliverable, current phase, reopenable decision set, accepted deferrals, and confirmation scope; preserving only the next question does not bound the work.
- P2. Approval-scope conflation: Rule-8 numeric selection confirm can be treated as artifact approval, phase completion, or permission to generate unrelated proposals; answer-confirm vs document-approve vs phase-complete are not separated in the continuation contract.
- P3. Handoff convention bleed: agent-authored handoffs can carry workflow conventions (for example mirror every confirmed decision into project/spec/six scopes and keep a pending proposal queue) that the operator did not authorize as Deft requirements, so continuation expands the proposal loop without a phase boundary.

related: #4668 (Depth preference persistence; distinct) #5176 (project-narrative persistence residual; distinct) #1709 (value-feedback filing path) interview Rules 6/7/8 setup Full output+review strategies/interview.md brownfield Update delta

## Prefer-A draft (charter target; not yet Bound)

**Bind Approach A.** Add a lightweight phase/continuation contract that reuses existing planning records where possible. Post-draft correction and cross-session resume restore deliverable, phase, decision set, deferrals, confirmations-with-scope, and the limited delta under review. Handoffs must distinguish human authorization from agent-created workflow conventions. Re-entry after artifact approval must not silently restart a full-depth interview. Existing operator authorization persists; do not add repeated permission prompts.

**Bound remedy limbs (draft):**
1. **Phase/continuation record.** Specify closed fields (or reuse of existing planning records) that name: target deliverable, current phase, reopenable decision set, accepted deferrals, and each confirmation with its scope (answer vs artifact vs phase). Incomplete orientation (next-question-only without a phase boundary) fails closed as incomplete handoff, not proof the workflow is sound.
2. **Delta reopen.** Changing one decision reopens that decision and demonstrable dependents only; unrelated backend/design proposals stay out of scope unless the operator widens the delta.
3. **Approval taxonomy.** Rule-8 numeric confirm records that choice only. Artifact approval and phase completion require their own explicit gates. Numeric confirm does not authorize implementation or unrelated proposal generation.
4. **Handoff authority split.** Handoffs must label human-authorized constraints separately from agent workflow conventions. Agent conventions are non-binding unless the operator adopts them. Continuation must not invent a mirror-every-decision / expand-proposal-queue duty as a Deft requirement.
5. **Two-session fixture.** Land regression evidence for same-session correction and a resumed session that restores deferred work and the bounded remaining decision set without restarting full-depth interview.
6. **Authorized incremental recordkeeping.** Keep lawful incremental updates that the operator already authorized; do not require one technical proposal per answer or copying every answer into every scope.

**Reject / defer:**
- Rewriting #4668 Depth-preference persistence or #5176 narrative-persistence residual (out of ownership).
- Adding new permission prompts that re-ask already-granted operator authorization.
- Treating the observed agent anti-pattern (questions+artifact generation) as excused by the gap; Prefer-A closes the state hole and keeps the existing anti-pattern forbid.

**arc-mode: no-ingest** for this arc. Ingest remains a later separate operator verb after completed-arc.

## Gate stamp

Fresh no-ingest yolo Stop 1 on #5352. Operator cue `arc using recommended n 5352` → parent recorded spend-recommend: N≥3 and took that recommend with spend-ask: asked (explicit use-recommended reply path). Charter is open critique of Prefer-A above. Dual-stop reserved literacy recorded. Next: N≥3 launch-probe + panel-deposit, then three-family round-1 critics, then Prefer-A Bound lean with honest pain cites, then reserved pain-audit of asserted coverage.

## Plain-language summary

#5352 closes a hole where design-interview revisions and handoffs lose the phase boundary and what was actually approved. Prefer-A adds a small continuation contract so corrections reopen only the affected decisions, numeric confirms stay answer-scoped, and handoffs separate human authorization from agent-invented workflow habits. Spend is N≥3 from the recorded recommend that you authorized with "use recommended."

F1. P2: distinguish the confirmation mechanism from the authority of the question being confirmed. Prefer-A's blanket statement that numeric confirmation records a choice only and cannot authorize implementation conflicts with an existing explicit approval menu: [strategy lines 550-595](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/strategies/interview.md#L550) offers numbered "Approve and continue (lock the SPEC, proceed to implementation)" and maps it to Accept. Meanwhile [Rule 8](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L267) describes the selection/confirmation mechanism, not a question-type discriminator. Define approval scope from the explicitly presented gate and its target, never from numeric syntax alone. An ordinary design answer must confer no artifact/build authority; a deliberately presented artifact gate must still work without an extra redundant permission prompt. For planning-only continuation, the existing combined approve/build label needs an explicit routing or precedence rule so artifact approval cannot silently override the planning-only constraint. Fixture: the same numeric response at a design question and at an explicit artifact gate must have different, declared effects.

F2. P1/P2: the proposed record needs an authoritative location and an approval target/revision, not merely a scope label. [Setup Full output lines 847-859](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md#L847) records approval "in the setup session" and subsequently generates scopes. [Continue-here lines 28-52](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/resilience/continue-here.md#L28) consumes the checkpoint on resume and distinguishes it from durable plans. Putting the new fields only in that checkpoint would leave the durable authority unclear after consumption; putting unversioned approval in a durable plan could falsely approve a later corrected artifact. Specify one durable owner, checkpoint reference, approval target and revision/change identity, and the effect of delta changes on existing approval. Preserve unchanged authorization; do not invalidate everything and ask again. Exercise a resume after checkpoint consumption and an artifact edit after approval, including an unchanged artifact whose approval remains valid.

F3. P1/P3: a named phase and reopenable set do not yet define a terminating review or constrain dependency expansion. [Rule 4 lines 123-127](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L123) keeps questioning until material ambiguity is gone; [Rule 6 lines 144-162](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L144) already limits corrections to specific questions. Yet [brownfield Update](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/strategies/interview.md#L94) does not bound the delta, and [Revise lines 562-564](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/strategies/interview.md#L562) returns to the chaining gate. Prefer-A must state which route wins on post-approval correction, what closes the current review, and what evidence makes a decision a demonstrable dependent. Otherwise an agent can call every new backend proposal a dependency and keep the same nominal phase forever. A small remedy suffices: identify the bounded delta, record a concrete dependency reason for additions, preserve accepted deferrals as non-blocking unless explicitly reopened, and stop when that delta's required decisions and review condition are satisfied. Include an adversarial fixture where a plausible but unrelated backend improvement is refused as an addition.

F4. P3: authority labels need a read-side consequence and evidence, particularly for legacy handoffs. [Continue-here lines 39-44](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/resilience/continue-here.md#L39) commands resuming from recorded decisions without re-debating them or reconstructing conversation. A handoff author can therefore label its own mirror-every-answer convention "human-authorized" and the receiving agent still inherits the same failure. Specify that authorization entries preserve a reference or faithful bounded excerpt of the actual operator grant; an agent's label alone is insufficient. Unattributed legacy workflow conventions should remain non-binding while verified existing grants remain effective. Also distinguish applicable framework obligations from discretionary agent conventions: the split must not accidentally demote actual rules. Test both a handoff containing only a next question and an unsupported authorization label; neither should generate new proposals or trigger a full interview restart. The incomplete-handoff remediation should recover only missing orientation, without re-asking established grants.

F5. P2/P3: Prefer-A's preservation of lawful incremental recordkeeping is sound, but the fixture must distinguish recording an answer from generating the reviewed artifact. [Rule 7 lines 178-195](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L178) hands an answers map to the caller; [anti-patterns lines 508-515](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L508) prohibit unconfirmed artifact generation and combining it with interview questions. Preserve that boundary explicitly when exercising authorized incremental writes. A positive test should record confirmed state under an existing grant without another permission prompt; a negative test should reject using that grant to synchronize unrelated scopes or generate an artifact alongside the next interview question. This supports limb 6 without excusing the reported anti-pattern.

## Open critique of Prefer-A (Stop 1 draft) vs P1–P3

Pin-read at `3456c6712614e352c5559b3c29caf9cbce26b5cf`: `content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md` (Rules 6/7/8, anti-patterns), `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` (Output — Full Path human approval; Post-Interview Confirmation Gate), `content/strategies/interview.md` (brownfield Update / delta), `content/resilience/continue-here.md` (nearby continuation/checkpoint helper).

Prefer-A's six limbs correctly name the Stop 1 holes. The pin confirms those holes are real. Prefer-A still underspecifies the binding surfaces enough that a faithful implementer could miss P1 durability, leave P2 gate reuse ambiguous, and leave P3 convention bleed as prose-only.

### F1 — P1 substrate unresolved (reuse-or-invent fork)

Limb 1 says "closed fields (or reuse of existing planning records)" without choosing a store.

- Rule 7 handoff is an answers map of field→value after Rule 6 passes (`deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md` Rule 7). It has no deliverable, current phase, reopenable set, deferrals, or confirmation-scope tags.
- `continue-here.md` already persists Completed / Remaining / Decisions / Resume point / planRef to `./xbrief/continue.xbrief.json`, but checkpoints are **ephemeral and consumed on resume**, and Resume point is "the exact first thing to do" — the same next-action-only shape Prefer-A wants to fail closed as incomplete handoff.
- Brownfield Update loads existing identity + preparatory artifacts (`interview.md` State Tracking) and runs a **delta** interview, with no durable post-draft decision-boundary fields.

Until Prefer-A picks durable store vs ephemeral continue-here vs Rule 7 expansion vs a new record, limb 1 does not relieve P1's cross-session hole. Reusing continue-here as-is would recreate next-question-only resume.

### F2 — P1 "fails closed" has no refuse surface

Limb 1: next-question-only without a phase boundary "fails closed as incomplete handoff." Pin has no interview/setup refuse, verifier, or skill-exit for that shape. Rule 7 only requires a complete answers map at interview-complete; incomplete mid-review orientation is not a named contract breach. Prefer-A must name the refuse (skill halt text, anti-pattern ⊗, or deterministic check) or the incomplete-handoff bar stays aspirational under P1.

### F3 — P1 "current phase" vocabulary unbound

Limb 1 requires a current-phase field. On pin, "phase" already means setup Phase 1/2/3, preparatory Research/Discuss/Probe/Map, and interview Rule 6→7 completion. Prefer-A does not close an enum for post-draft states the report cares about (e.g. planning-draft-approved, correction/gap-review, artifact-approved, deferred-resume). Without that closed set, agents invent free-text phase labels and P1 resume stays unbounded.

### F4 — P2 approval taxonomy correct in intent, underspecified in gate reuse

Limb 3 correctly scopes Rule 8: pin Rule 8 is echo-selection + Enter before the next question only; it does not authorize artifact write or phase exit.

Existing distinct gates on pin:

- Rule 6 Confirmation Gate — summary of all answers; yes/no before artifact generation; correction re-asks named fields only (`interview` Rule 6).
- Setup Post-Interview Confirmation Gate — "Write files? (yes/no)" before USER.md / PROJECT-DEFINITION / scope writes.
- Setup Output — Full Path step 2 **Human approval gate** — present PROJECT-DEFINITION narratives + proposed scope plan for review; "Record approval in the setup session."

Limb 3 says artifact approval and phase completion need "their own explicit gates" but does not bind those gates to the three above vs invent new ones. Without that bind-map, a continuation can keep using Rule-8 confirms as the practical workflow unit (P2) while claiming a separate taxonomy in prose. Prefer-A should say which existing gate is artifact approval, which is phase completion, and what (if anything) is new for post-draft gap-review exit.

### F5 — P2 confirmation-with-scope has no recording schema

Limb 1 wants each confirmation tagged answer vs artifact vs phase. Pin answers map and continue-here Decisions are unscoped narratives/values. Accepted deferrals stay non-blocking unless explicitly reopened. Terminating condition: stop when the bounded delta's required decisions and review condition are satisfied. Framework obligations stay distinct from discretionary agent conventions (do not demote real rules).

That grant does not authorize synchronizing unrelated scopes or generating an artifact alongside the next interview question. 8. **Landing surfaces.** Primary: interview skill (pack + rendered), setup Full output/review / Post-Interview gate pointers, strategies/interview.md brownfield Update / delta continuation, continue-here.md explicit exclusion + pointer to durable carrier, plan.xbrief.json schema/field docs.    - Do not rewrite #4668 Depth-preference persistence or #5176 narrative-persistence residual (orthogonal ownership).

metadata.issueBody:
## Summary

Design interview revisions and handoffs do not preserve a bounded phase and approval scope

## Context

Observed during an operator-directed Full design interview for an existing application, followed by a continuation session. The operator requested planning only, preservation of existing changes, and no implementation. The first artifact batch was explicitly approved; later backend and gap reviews were also requested. This report does not characterize all technical questions or artifact writes as unauthorized.

The consumer engine and content deposit were 0.119.12. The relevant interview/strategy content was also compared with a 0.120.0 deposit. On 2026-10-04, the cited rules were verified on upstream master at `3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820`. Session examples below come from a local conversation audit; private project files and raw chat logs are not published.

## Expected behavior

After an approved planning draft, a correction or gap review should reopen the affected decisions with an explicit phase boundary. A continuation should preserve the target deliverable, unresolved material decisions, approval scope, and deferrals, rather than inheriting an indefinitely expanding proposal loop.

## Actual behavior / gap

The interview has a summary gate and an answers-map exit, and brownfield setup has a delta-interview route. The inspected contract does not specify sufficient state for prolonged post-draft review and cross-session continuation. A numeric selection confirmation can become the practical workflow unit while the distinction between answer approval, document approval, and phase completion is lost.

In the observed sequence, the agent repeatedly recorded one confirmed answer, synchronized multiple artifacts, prepared the next technical proposal, and asked for its adoption. The handoff preserved the current pending queue contract and a convention to mirror every confirmed decision into the project, specification, and six scopes. The continuation followed that convention and created five further proposals before the operator challenged the process. The handoff was agent-authored and operator-requested; its detailed convention was not a generic Deft requirement.

## Session notes

### Source evidence

- [Rule 6 confirmation and Rule 7 exit](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L142) distinguish final summary confirmation and an answers-map handoff.
- [Rule 8](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L267) confirms an individual numeric choice.
- [Brownfield Update path](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820/content/strategies/interview.md#L94) calls for a delta interview, but does not define the reviewed delta's durable decision boundary across sessions.
- [Full output and review](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820/content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md#L847) define artifact review but not the extended review/continuation state observed here.
- [Anti-pattern](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/3d613b146a3880ecb261bf8654d7abe73b498820/content/skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md#L515) already forbids combining artifact generation with interview questions. The agent violated this rule; this report does not excuse that violation.

### Reproduction scenario

1. Complete a consolidated interview summary and receive authorization to write a planning draft.
2. Receive a correction or a request to inspect gaps, then resolve several specific decisions.
3. Prepare a handoff naming the last confirmed answer, next pending proposal, and existing artifact-update conventions.
4. Resume in a fresh session with 'continue the interview from its checkpoint.'
5. Observe that preserving the next question is insufficient to establish the current phase, what counts as completion, which decisions may be reopened, or whether new proposals remain in scope.

### Requested remedy

Specify a lightweight phase/continuation contract using existing planning records where possible. Preserve the deliverable, current phase, decision set, accepted deferrals, confirmations with their scope, and the limited delta being reviewed. A handoff must distinguish human authorization from agent-created workflow conventions. Re-entry after artifact approval should not silently restart a full-depth interview. Existing operator authorization must persist; do not add repeated permission prompts.

### Acceptance and regression evidence

- Changing one UI decision reopens that decision and demonstrable dependents, not unrelated backend design.
- Confirming a numeric choice records that choice; it does not imply final artifact approval, implementation authorization, or permission to generate unrelated proposals.
- A resumed session restores deferred work and the bounded remaining decision set.
- A handoff that contains a next question but lacks a phase boundary is treated as incomplete orientation, not proof that the workflow is sound.
- Authorized incremental recordkeeping still works; the fix does not require one technical proposal per answer or copying every answer to every scope.
- Exercise a two-session fixture in addition to same-session corrections.

### Scope and prior art

Distinct from the completion/materiality defect: this report owns approval scope, delta reopening, and continuation state. The body and comments of #4668 were reviewed: its delivered remedy persists the Phase 2 Depth preference and skips re-asking it; its separate project-narrative persistence residual moved to #5176. This report concerns expanding post-draft review and carrying that expansion into another session, not either persistence remedy. No implementation or scope promotion is requested by this report. Refs #1709.
